symbols.name: \underline y
symbols.role: Lower endpoint of the maintained outcome support.

symbols.name: \overline y
symbols.role: Upper endpoint of the maintained outcome support.

symbols.name: \mathcal H
symbols.role: Set of realized finite scheduled first-implementation cohorts.

symbols.name: \mathcal R
symbols.def: \(\mathcal R=\mathcal H\cup\{\infty\}\), where a finite index is a first-implementation date and \(\infty\) indexes the path with neither announcement nor implementation during the study.
symbols.role: Index set for canonical announced-policy regime paths.

symbols.name: r
symbols.role: Generic canonical regime-path index, with finite \(r\) denoting first implementation at \(r\).

symbols.name: \mathsf a
symbols.def: \(\mathsf a(r)<r\) is the fixed public announcement or policy-decision date attached to every finite implementation date \(r\in\mathcal H\).

symbols.name: p^r
symbols.def: For every finite \(r\in\mathcal H\), \(p^r\) is the complete canonical policy path whose announcement or decision occurs at \(\mathsf a(r)\), whose implementation status is zero at every \(t<r\), and whose first implementation occurs at \(r\) and remains in force thereafter. Announcement content and implemented-policy content are fixed components of this known path. The path \(p^\infty\) has neither announcement nor implementation at any \(t\in\mathcal T\). The mapping \(r\mapsto p^r\) is deterministic and known.

symbols.name: G
symbols.role: Realized first-implementation cohort; units with \(G=r\) realize the complete canonical path \(p^r\).

symbols.name: Y_t(p^r)
symbols.def: \(Y_t(p^r)\) is the period-\(t\) potential outcome under the complete canonical regime path \(p^r\); \(Y_t(p^\infty)\) is the outcome under neither announcement nor implementation.

symbols.name: D_t
symbols.def: \(D_t=\mathbf 1\{G\le t\}\), with \(\infty\not\le t\).

symbols.name: O
symbols.def: \(O=(G,(Y_t,D_t)_{t\in\mathcal T})\).

symbols.name: P_{\mathrm{obs}}
symbols.def: \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}=\mathcal L(O)\).

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: \(P\) is one joint law of \(G\) and all \(\{Y_t(p^r):t\in\mathcal T,r\in\mathcal R\}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal E
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E=\{(h,t)\in\mathcal H\times\mathcal T:t<h\}\); thus every observed cell before its finite scheduled implementation is included.

symbols.name: e
symbols.def: For \(e=(h,t)\), write \(h(e)=h\) and \(t(e)=t\).

symbols.name: \mathcal E_0
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E_0=\{(h,t)\in\mathcal E:t<\mathsf a(h)\}\), the preannouncement cells of the canonical paths.

symbols.name: \mathcal E_A
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E_A=\{(h,t)\in\mathcal E:\mathsf a(h)\le t<h\}=\mathcal E\setminus\mathcal E_0\).

symbols.name: \mu
symbols.def: \(\mu_e=E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}[Y_{t(e)}\mid G=h(e)]\).

symbols.name: \ell
symbols.def: \(\ell_e=0\) for \(e=(h,t)\) with \(t<\mathsf a(h)\); for \(\mathsf a(h)\le t<h\), \(\ell_e\) is the preregistered lower bound on the mean effect of path \(p^h\) relative to \(p^\infty\) at \(t\).

symbols.name: u
symbols.def: \(u_e=0\) for \(e=(h,t)\) with \(t<\mathsf a(h)\); for \(\mathsf a(h)\le t<h\), \(u_e\) is the preregistered upper bound on the mean effect of path \(p^h\) relative to \(p^\infty\) at \(t\).

symbols.name: \mathcal V
symbols.def: \(\mathcal V=\mathcal H\sqcup\mathcal T\).

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: \(c\) is the number of connected components of \((\mathcal V,\mathcal E)\).
symbols.role: Component count governing the fixed-effect gauges.

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: The column of \(B\) for \(e=(h,t)\) has \(+1\) at cohort vertex \(h\), \(-1\) at time vertex \(t\), and zero elsewhere.

symbols.name: C
symbols.def: Choose a spanning forest and let the rows of \(C\) be its signed fundamental-cycle vectors, so \(CB^{\mathsf T}=0\) and \(\ker(C)=\operatorname{im}(B^{\mathsf T})\).

symbols.name: \mathcal W
symbols.def: \(\mathcal W=\{e\in\mathcal E:u_e>\ell_e\}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal F
symbols.def: \(\mathcal F=\mathcal E\setminus\mathcal W\).
symbols.role: Fixed, including clean and zero-width, coordinates.

symbols.name: \overline a_{\mathcal F}
symbols.def: \((\overline a_{\mathcal F})_e=\ell_e=u_e\) for \(e\in\mathcal F\).

symbols.name: \alpha_h
symbols.role: Cohort component of the conditional mean under the path with neither announcement nor implementation.

symbols.name: \lambda_t
symbols.role: Calendar-time component of the conditional mean under the path with neither announcement nor implementation.

symbols.name: \beta
symbols.def: \(\beta_h=\alpha_h\) on cohort vertices and \(\beta_t=-\lambda_t\) on time vertices, so \((B^{\mathsf T}\beta)_{(h,t)}=\alpha_h+\lambda_t\).

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: \(a_e=E_P[Y_{t(e)}(p^{h(e)})-Y_{t(e)}(p^\infty)\mid G=h(e)]\).

symbols.name: \mathcal A_{\mathrm{cyc}}(\mu)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{cyc}}(\mu)=\{a\in\prod_{e\in\mathcal E}[\ell_e,u_e]:Ca=C\mu\}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal I(\mu)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I(\mu)=\{e\in\mathcal W:\text{ there exist }a,a'\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{cyc}}(\mu)\text{ with }a_e\ne a'_e\}\).
symbols.role: Coordinates of the minimal box face that genuinely vary within the nonempty cycle fiber.

symbols.name: \mathcal K
symbols.def: \(\mathcal K=\mathcal H\times\mathcal T\), oriented from cohort to time.
symbols.role: Complete cohort--time edge set used to enforce bounded means under the path with neither announcement nor implementation.

symbols.name: k
symbols.role: Generic complete cohort--time edge used for bounded baseline means.

symbols.name: B^+
symbols.def: \(B^+\) is the oriented incidence matrix of the multigraph with edge multiset \(\mathcal E\sqcup\mathcal K\).
symbols.role: Augmented incidence matrix for observed restrictions and bounded causal completion.

symbols.name: d^-
symbols.def: For the copy of \(e\in\mathcal E\), \(d^-_e=\mu_e-u_e\); for \(k\in\mathcal K\), \(d^-_k=\underline y\).

symbols.name: d^+
symbols.def: For the copy of \(e\in\mathcal E\), \(d^+_e=\mu_e-\ell_e\); for \(k\in\mathcal K\), \(d^+_k=\overline y\).

symbols.name: \mathcal D(d^-,d^+)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal D(d^-,d^+)\) has vertex set \(\mathcal V\); each augmented edge oriented from cohort vertex \(h\) to time vertex \(t\) contributes an arc \(t\to h\) of weight \(d^+_e\) and an arc \(h\to t\) of weight \(-d^-_e\).

symbols.name: \mathcal Q_Y(\mu)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal Q_Y(\mu)=\{\beta:d^-\le (B^+)^{\mathsf T}\beta\le d^+\}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal A_Y(\mu)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal A_Y(\mu)=\{\mu-B^{\mathsf T}\beta:\beta\in\mathcal Q_Y(\mu)\}\).
symbols.role: Cycle-compatible anticipation fiber admitting bounded baseline means at every cohort--time cell.

symbols.name: \mathfrak M(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak M(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) is the set of full announced-policy laws that project to \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) and satisfy the maintained causal restrictions.

symbols.name: t_j
symbols.role: Post-implementation period for target \(j\), with \(t_j\ge g_j\).

symbols.name: b_j
symbols.role: Chosen clean base period for target \(j\).

symbols.name: q_j
symbols.role: Chosen not-yet-treated comparison cohort for target \(j\).

symbols.name: \mathsf{RA}
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{RA}\) holds when, for every \(j\in\mathcal J\), \(b_j<g_j\le t_j<q_j\), the three edges \((g_j,b_j),(q_j,b_j),(q_j,t_j)\) belong to \(\mathcal E_0\), and \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}(G=q_j)>0\).
symbols.role: Rectangular risk-set anchoring condition for the zero-anticipation sanity reduction.

symbols.name: \nu_j
symbols.def: \(\nu_j=E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}[Y_{t_j}\mid G=g_j]\).

symbols.name: s_j
symbols.def: \(s_j\) has \(+1\) at cohort vertex \(g_j\), \(-1\) at time vertex \(t_j\), and zero elsewhere.

symbols.name: s(w)
symbols.def: \(s(w)=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}w_js_j\).
symbols.role: Node-balance vector induced by the ATT aggregate.

symbols.name: x^+
symbols.role: Positive-direction split flow in the transshipment dual.

symbols.name: x^-
symbols.role: Negative-direction split flow in the transshipment dual.

symbols.name: \theta_j
symbols.def: \(\theta_j=E_P[Y_{t_j}(p^{g_j})-Y_{t_j}(p^\infty)\mid G=g_j]\).
symbols.role: Group--time average effect of the cohort's canonical announcement-and-implementation path relative to neither announcement nor implementation.

symbols.name: \theta_w
symbols.def: \(\theta_w=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}w_j\theta_j\).

symbols.name: \Theta_I(w;P_{\mathrm{obs}})
symbols.type: closed subset of the real line
symbols.def: \(\Theta_I(w;P_{\mathrm{obs}})=\{\theta_w(P):P\in\mathfrak M(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\}\).
symbols.role: Causal identified set for the aggregate.

symbols.name: \mathfrak W_3
symbols.role: Three-cohort shared-comparison instance used to audit the strict contraction calculation.

symbols.name: \psi_3
symbols.role: Equal-weight mean anticipation distortion in the two focal cohort--time cells.

symbols.name: z
symbols.role: Common free anticipation level in the worked instance.

symbols.name: \mathsf{Comp}_3(z)
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{Comp}_3(z)\) requires one joint law of \(G\) and all regime-path potential outcomes to project to the observed law of \(\mathfrak W_3\), to satisfy \(E_P[Y_2(p^\infty)\mid G=h]=2\) and \(E_P[Y_3(p^\infty)\mid G=h]=2-z\) for \(h\in\{4,5,6\}\), and to realize \((a_{4,3},a_{5,3},a_{6,3})=(z+1/2,z,z)\) with \(a_{h,2}=0\).
symbols.role: Explicit regime-path potential-outcome completion target associated with the worked observed law.

symbols.name: \operatorname{MC}(b;d^-,d^+)
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{MC}(b;d^-,d^+)=\min_{x^+,x^-\ge0}\{(d^+)^{\mathsf T}x^+-(d^-)^{\mathsf T}x^-:B^+(x^+-x^-)=b\}\).
symbols.role: Minimum-cost transshipment value with split directed flows.

symbols.name: L_w
symbols.def: \(L_w\) is the lower endpoint of \(\Theta_I(w;P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).
symbols.role: Sharp lower endpoint for the signed ATT aggregate.

symbols.name: U_w
symbols.def: \(U_w\) is the upper endpoint of \(\Theta_I(w;P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).
symbols.role: Sharp upper endpoint for the signed ATT aggregate.

symbols.name: N_h
symbols.def: \(N_h=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{G_i=h\}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\mu
symbols.def: \(\widehat\mu_e=N_{h(e)}^{-1}\sum_{i:G_i=h(e)}Y_{i,t(e)}\) when \(N_{h(e)}>0\).

symbols.name: \widehat\nu
symbols.def: \(\widehat\nu_j=N_{g_j}^{-1}\sum_{i:G_i=g_j}Y_{i,t_j}\) when \(N_{g_j}>0\).

symbols.name: \rho_h
symbols.def: For \(N_h>0\), \(\rho_h=(\overline y-\underline y)\sqrt{\log(2(|\mathcal E|+|\mathcal J|)/\eta)/(2N_h)}\); for \(N_h=0\), \(\rho_h=\overline y-\underline y\).

symbols.name: \mathcal R_{1-\eta}
symbols.def: \(\mathcal R_{1-\eta}\) is the Cartesian product of \([\widehat\mu_e-\rho_{h(e)},\widehat\mu_e+\rho_{h(e)}]\cap[\underline y,\overline y]\) and \([\widehat\nu_j-\rho_{g_j},\widehat\nu_j+\rho_{g_j}]\cap[\underline y,\overline y]\), using \([\underline y,\overline y]\) when the relevant cohort count is zero.

symbols.name: \widehat\Theta^{\mathrm{out}}_{1-\eta}(w)
symbols.type: random closed subset of the real line
symbols.def: \(\widehat\Theta^{\mathrm{out}}_{1-\eta}(w)=\bigcup_{(\mu',\nu')\in\mathcal R_{1-\eta}}\{\sum_jw_j\nu'_j-s(w)^{\mathsf T}\beta:\beta\in\mathcal Q_Y(\mu')\}\).
symbols.role: Jointly optimized finite-sample outer confidence set.

assumptions.condition: \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}(G=h)>0\) for every cohort vertex incident to an edge in \(\mathcal E\) or used by a target in \(\mathcal J\).
\(Y_t=Y_t(p^G)\) almost surely for every \(t\in\mathcal T\), where units with \(G=r\) realize the complete canonical path \(p^r\).

standard.name: Intervention-indexed consistency for an announced policy

novel.justification: This is a proposal-specific all-cohort additive mean restriction, not a maintained condition attributed to Callaway--Sant'Anna. Under the canonical path with neither announcement nor implementation, scheduled cohorts may differ in mean outcome levels but share calendar-time mean movements; this interpretation can be assessed on cells preceding the known dates \(\mathsf a(h)\). A single collection of cohort and time effects is substantively needed when the same future-treated comparison cell is reused in several risk sets, because otherwise those uses need not correspond to one coherent no-announcement mean surface.

This is a proposal-specific edgewise sensitivity restriction, distinct from Fenaroli's cohort-level bounds on anticipation-related increments. The application protocol records the public decision date \(\mathsf a(h)\) and implementation date \(h\) for every canonical cohort path, declares \(t<\mathsf a(h)\) clean, and preregisters a separate interval \([\ell_e,u_e]\) for each announcement-to-implementation cell \(\mathsf a(h)\le t<h\). Each interval is calibrated on the outcome scale from subject-matter limits on the largest plausible response to that announced path, supplemented where available by placebo shifts from comparable preannouncement cohorts; asymmetric responses are represented by asymmetric endpoints.

assumptions.condition: \(Y_t(p^r)\in[\underline y,\overline y]\) almost surely for every \((t,r)\in\mathcal T\times\mathcal R\).

definitions.name: Fundamental-cycle anticipation fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{cyc}}(\mu)=\{a\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal E}:\ell_e\le a_e\le u_e\text{ for every }e\in\mathcal E,\ Ca=C\mu\}\).

definitions.name: Varying coordinates of the minimal box face
definitions.construction: For a nonempty fiber, \(\mathcal I(\mu)=\{e\in\mathcal W:\exists a,a'\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{cyc}}(\mu)\text{ such that }a_e\ne a'_e\}\); coordinates outside \(\mathcal I(\mu)\) are fixed throughout the fiber.

definitions.name: Rectangular not-yet-treated anchor
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{RA}\) holds if and only if there exist choices \((b_j,q_j)_{j\in\mathcal J}\) such that \(b_j<g_j\le t_j<q_j\), \((g_j,b_j),(q_j,b_j),(q_j,t_j)\in\mathcal E_0\), and \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}(G=q_j)>0\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\).

definitions.name: Fully specified rational three-cohort witness \(\mathfrak W_3\)
definitions.construction: In \(\mathfrak W_3\), set \(\mathcal H=\{4,5,6\}\), \(\mathcal T=\{2,3\}\), \(\mathsf a(h)=3\) for every \(h\in\mathcal H\), \([\underline y,\overline y]=[0,4]\), and hence \(\mathcal E=\mathcal H\times\mathcal T\). The known path \(p^h\) announces at date \(3\), has no implementation before \(h\), and first implements at \(h\); \(p^\infty\) has neither event. Let \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}(G=h)=1/3\) for each \(h\in\mathcal H\), let \(Y_2=2\) almost surely, and let \(Y_3=5/2\) on \(G=4\) and \(Y_3=2\) on \(G\in\{5,6\}\). Set \(\mathcal E_0=\{(4,2),(5,2),(6,2)\}\), set \(\ell_e=u_e=0\) on \(\mathcal E_0\), and set \([\ell_e,u_e]=[-1,1]\) on \(e\in\{(4,3),(5,3),(6,3)\}\). Finally set \(\psi_3=(a_{4,3}+a_{5,3})/2\).

definitions.name: Worked-instance full-law completion target
definitions.construction: For \(z\in[-1,1/2]\), \(\mathsf{Comp}_3(z)\) is the set of joint laws \(P\) of \(G\) and all \(\{Y_t(p^r):t\in\mathcal T,r\in\mathcal R\}\) that project to the observed law in \(\mathfrak W_3\), satisfy consistency along \(p^G\), satisfy \(E_P[Y_2(p^\infty)\mid G=h]=2\) and \(E_P[Y_3(p^\infty)\mid G=h]=2-z\) for every \(h\in\{4,5,6\}\), and realize \((a_{4,3},a_{5,3},a_{6,3})=(z+1/2,z,z)\) and \(a_{h,2}=0\).

definitions.name: Bounded-outcome interval-tension completion
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal Q_Y(\mu)=\{\beta\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal V}:\mu_e-u_e\le(B^{\mathsf T}\beta)_e\le\mu_e-\ell_e\text{ for }e\in\mathcal E,\ \underline y\le\alpha_h+\lambda_t\le\overline y\text{ for }(h,t)\in\mathcal K\}\), and \(\mathcal A_Y(\mu)=\{\mu-B^{\mathsf T}\beta:\beta\in\mathcal Q_Y(\mu)\}\).

definitions.name: Split-flow transshipment functional
definitions.construction: For any component-balanced \(b\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal V}\), \(\operatorname{MC}(b;d^-,d^+)=\min_{x^+,x^-\ge0}\{(d^+)^{\mathsf T}x^+-(d^-)^{\mathsf T}x^-:B^+(x^+-x^-)=b\}\).

definitions.name: Conditional endpoint-mixture causal-completion handle
definitions.construction: Retain the complete observed outcome vector under its realized canonical path \(p^G\); use common conditional latent uniforms to construct the unobserved \(p^\infty\) vector and every off-path \(p^r\) vector with prescribed cohort--time means; use one gauge per connected component before the mixture step to meet the bounded-support inequalities.

definitions.name: Finite-sample simultaneous bounded-mean rectangle
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal R_{1-\eta}=\prod_{e\in\mathcal E}([\widehat\mu_e-\rho_{h(e)},\widehat\mu_e+\rho_{h(e)}]\cap[\underline y,\overline y])\times\prod_{j\in\mathcal J}([\widehat\nu_j-\rho_{g_j},\widehat\nu_j+\rho_{g_j}]\cap[\underline y,\overline y])\), with a zero-count factor replaced by \([\underline y,\overline y]\).

statements.statement: For every \(a\in\prod_{e\in\mathcal E}[\ell_e,u_e]\), there exists a vertex potential \(\beta\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal V}\) satisfying \(\mu=B^{\mathsf T}\beta+a\) if and only if \(Ca=C\mu\). Consequently, the set of all anticipation vectors admitting the proposal-specific all-cohort additive decomposition is exactly \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{cyc}}(\mu)\). If this fiber is nonempty, its affine dimension is \[\dim\operatorname{aff}\mathcal A_{\mathrm{cyc}}(\mu)=|\mathcal I(\mu)|-\operatorname{rank}(C_{\mathcal I(\mu)}).\] In the relative-interior case \(\mathcal I(\mu)=\mathcal W\), this reduces to \(|\mathcal W|-\operatorname{rank}(C_{\mathcal W})\). The face-correct formula remains valid for disconnected graphs, zero-width edges, and fibers lying on proper box faces.
statements.justification: The theorem turns reused not-yet-treated cells into an explicit, basis-invariant joint restriction rather than an assumed Cartesian box.
statements.gap: Fenaroli2026, Section 4.2 fixes never-treated controls and observes that using not-yet-treated comparisons requires accounting for anticipation in the comparison group; it does not characterize the compatibility restrictions created when such cells are reused across risk sets. JochmansWeidner2019, Section 2 supplies incidence and component-gauge algebra but no anticipation identified set.
statements.consumer: A Callaway--Sant'Anna risk-set audit can report the exact number and location of anticipation degrees of freedom before any ATT aggregation is computed.

statements.statement: The primitive anticipation coordinates are variation independent, \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{cyc}}(\mu)=\prod_{e\in\mathcal E}[\ell_e,u_e]\), if and only if \(C_{\mathcal W}=0\) and \(C_{\mathcal F}\overline a_{\mathcal F}=C\mu\). Equivalently, fixed coordinates satisfy every fixed-cycle equation and every positive-width edge in \(\mathcal W\) is a bridge of \((\mathcal V,\mathcal E)\).
statements.justification: The bridge frontier gives a design-level if-and-only-if answer to when an uncoupled independent-box analysis is exact.
statements.gap: Dawid2001 defines variation independence as a product-range property. No located DiD result links that property to bridges in a cohort--time anticipation graph.
statements.consumer: Researchers choosing not-yet-treated controls can determine from the risk-set graph alone whether cellwise sensitivity analysis is jointly coherent.

statements.statement: For any \(e_0\in\mathcal W\), the nominal lower endpoint \(a_{e_0}=\ell_{e_0}\) is attained in \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{cyc}}(\mu)\) if and only if the interval-tension system obtained by replacing \([\ell_{e_0},u_{e_0}]\) with \([\ell_{e_0},\ell_{e_0}]\) contains a vertex potential. This holds if and only if its two-arc difference-constraint digraph has no negative directed cycle. The analogous equivalence with \([u_{e_0},u_{e_0}]\) characterizes upper-endpoint attainment; applying the same test to the augmented edge multiset \(\mathcal E\sqcup\mathcal K\) characterizes endpoint exactness in \(\mathcal A_Y(\mu)\).
statements.justification: Coordinatewise sharpness can fail even when the joint fiber is nonempty, so the endpoint certificate prevents reporting unattainable box extremes.
statements.gap: Fenaroli2026 derives closed-form cohortwise endpoints under never-treated comparison groups. No adjacent anticipation paper provides a necessary-and-sufficient negative-cycle certificate after a comparison cohort is reused across risk sets.
statements.consumer: Sensitivity tables for the Indonesian anti-cheating rollout can flag which nominal cohort-year anticipation bounds are actually reachable under all shared comparisons.

statements.statement: Does the conditional endpoint-mixture causal-completion handle establish the following exhaustive extension property? For every \(a\in\mathcal A_Y(\mu)\), every observed law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) satisfying the support and overlap conditions, and a corresponding \(\beta\in\mathcal Q_Y(\mu)\) with \(a=\mu-B^{\mathsf T}\beta\), construct one joint law \(P\in\mathfrak M(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) of \(G\) and all \(\{Y_t(p^r):t\in\mathcal T,r\in\mathcal R\}\) that preserves the entire joint distribution of \(O\), realizes the same \(a\) and \(\beta\), satisfies consistency along the realized complete path \(p^G\), and simultaneously defines every \(\theta_j=E_P[Y_{t_j}(p^{g_j})-Y_{t_j}(p^\infty)\mid G=g_j]=\nu_j-s_j^{\mathsf T}\beta\) for \(j\in\mathcal J\). The worked diagnostic requires, in particular, deciding whether \(\mathsf{Comp}_3(z)\neq\varnothing\) for every \(z\in[-1,1/2]\). If the general property fails, characterize the smallest additional cross-path compatibility inequality and a minimal graph counterexample.
statements.justification: Mean feasibility is not causal sharpness until every feasible mean vector is lifted to one common bounded full-data law indexed by fully specified announcement-and-implementation paths.
statements.gap: Torgovitsky2019 proves sharpness by extending lower-dimensional distributional objects, and PiccininniTchetgenStensrud2025 shows why the intervention being anticipated must be explicit. Neither paper supplies a staggered completion over one known canonical path per implementation cohort with overlapping comparison cohorts.
statements.consumer: A positive resolution makes every reported endpoint an attainable announced-policy ATT, while a negative resolution supplies the missing restriction needed by all bounded-anticipation risk-set analyses.

statements.statement: If the exhaustive extension property in Open-ended Question 1 holds, then for every signed weight vector \(w\), \[\Theta_I(w;P_{\mathrm{obs}})=\left\{\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}w_j\nu_j-s(w)^{\mathsf T}\beta:\beta\in\mathcal Q_Y(\mu)\right\}.\] Hence the joint identified region for \((\theta_j)_{j\in\mathcal J}\) is exactly the affine image of \(\mathcal Q_Y(\mu)\), and every exposed endpoint is attained by one full law rather than by target-specific laws.
statements.justification: This is the causal sharpness payoff: one polyhedral object supports all overlapping group--time effects and all signed aggregates.
statements.gap: CallawaySantAnna2021, Theorem 1 point-identifies each group--time effect after choosing clean never- or not-yet-treated comparisons. Gong2022 and Fenaroli2026 bound anticipation in smaller or never-treated settings; none gives a joint causal fiber for contaminated not-yet-treated controls.
statements.consumer: The result replaces a collection of separately computed sensitivity intervals by one coherent identified region for event-time, group, and calendar-time summaries.

statements.statement:
If the exhaustive extension property in Open-ended Question 1 holds and \(\mathcal Q_Y(\mu)
eq\varnothing\), then for every signed \(w\), the sharp aggregate endpoints in Theorem 4 equal \[L_w=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}w_j
u_j-\operatorname{MC}(s(w);d^-,d^+),\qquad U_w=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}w_j
u_j+\operatorname{MC}(-s(w);d^-,d^+).\] Primal and dual optimizers recover an attaining fixed-effect potential and anticipation vector. Feasibility of \(\mathcal Q_Y(\mu)\) is equivalent to absence of a negative directed cycle in the augmented interval-tension digraph.
statements.justification: The transshipment dual makes arbitrary policy-relevant ATT summaries sharp, auditable, and computationally scalable without assuming coordinatewise independence.
statements.gap: Voronin2025 studies generic stochastic LP values and ChenKyngLiuPengProbstGutenbergSachdeva2022 solves general minimum-cost flow. No located DiD paper derives this node-balance dual from a coupled anticipation fiber; uncoupled cellwise optimization does not deliver its joint support values.
statements.consumer: The Callaway--Sant'Anna aggregation step can obtain exact event-time or calendar-time sensitivity endpoints and a dual certificate from the same risk-set graph.

statements.statement: If the exhaustive extension property in Open-ended Question 1 holds, then under independent sampling and bounded potential outcomes, for every fixed signed \(w\), \[\inf_{P\in\mathfrak M(P_{\mathrm{obs}})}P^n\left\{\Theta_I(w;P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq\widehat\Theta^{\mathrm{out}}_{1-\eta}(w)\right\}\ge1-\eta.\] The two endpoints of \(\widehat\Theta^{\mathrm{out}}_{1-\eta}(w)\) are obtained by one joint interval-tension optimization: replace each observed-edge tension by \([\widehat\mu_e-\rho_{h(e)}-u_e,\widehat\mu_e+\rho_{h(e)}-\ell_e]\cap[\underline y-u_e,\overline y-\ell_e]\), retain the bounded-baseline tensions, and optimize the simultaneous target-mean bands with the signed weights. The claim remains valid when the population fiber is a singleton, when optimizer faces change, and when some sample cohort counts are zero.
statements.justification: Coverage follows from one simultaneous primitive-mean event and therefore survives the nonsmooth feasibility and active-face changes of the identified region.
statements.gap: CallawaySantAnna2021 gives asymptotic multiplier bands, FangLiebl2026 gives functional asymptotic bands, and Fenaroli2026 reports Bayesian credible bands for nonsmooth bounds. None gives finite-sample frequentist outer coverage for a cycle-coupled ATT region.
statements.consumer: Applications with bounded test scores, including the Indonesian computer-testing rollout, obtain an honest finite-sample sensitivity region without bootstrapping unstable endpoint maps.

statements.statement: The construction has the following exact sanity reductions. First, if \(\ell=u=0\), \(C\mu=0\), and the rectangular anchor \(\mathsf{RA}\) holds, then \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{cyc}}(\mu)=\{0\}\) and each target is point identified by the usual not-yet-treated two-by-two functional \[\theta_j=(\nu_j-\mu_{(g_j,b_j)})-(\mu_{(q_j,t_j)}-\mu_{(q_j,b_j)}).\] Second, if every positive-width edge is a bridge and the bounded-baseline inequalities are slack throughout the primitive box, the bridge frontier and the transshipment support values reduce to the independent-box calculation. Third, order a four-cycle so \(C=(1,-1,1,-1)\), give its first and third coordinates intervals \([0,1]\), fix its second and fourth coordinates at zero, and set \(C\mu=0\). Then the fiber is \(\{0\}\), \(\mathcal I(\mu)=\varnothing\), and the corrected dimension is \(0=|\mathcal I(\mu)|-\operatorname{rank}(C_{\mathcal I(\mu)})\); the unqualified positive-width expression would instead equal \(2-1=1\). Finally, in \(\mathfrak W_3\), the cycle equations give \[\mathcal A_{\mathrm{cyc}}(\mu)=\{a:a_{h,2}=0,\ (a_{4,3},a_{5,3},a_{6,3})=(z+1/2,z,z),\ -1\le z\le1/2\}.\] Therefore \(a_{4,3}-a_{5,3}=1/2\) and the exact support of \(\psi_3\) is \([-3/4,3/4]\), whereas optimizing the same equal-weight functional over the uncoupled primitive box gives \([-1,1]\).
statements.justification: The proposition verifies the anchored no-anticipation corner, the boundary-face dimension correction, and the strict coupled contraction by direct rational calculations.
statements.gap: CallawaySantAnna2021 supplies the anchored zero-anticipation two-by-two functional, while no published source records the face-correct dimension diagnostic or the fully specified three-cohort contraction induced by shared anticipatory cells.
statements.consumer: The four-cycle and three-cohort calculations are exact unit tests for dimension and endpoint software, and the anchor condition prevents a disconnected target gauge from being mislabeled as point identified.

sampling_model.design: Finite-period staggered adoption with a fixed, known canonical mapping from each implementation date to one complete announcement-and-implementation path, together with a fixed collection of not-yet-treated comparison risk sets.
sampling_model.units: Independent superpopulation draws of the complete observed panel vector; the number of periods and cohorts is fixed.
sampling_model.treatment: For cohort \(h\), the policy is announced or decided at known date \(\mathsf a(h)<h\), is not implemented before \(h\), and is first implemented at \(h\) and remains in force thereafter; outcomes may respond between \(\mathsf a(h)\) and \(h-1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every cohort used by an observed graph edge or target has positive population probability; zero realized sample counts receive the full outcome-support band.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cohort--time means are estimated by sample averages and enclosed jointly by bounded-mean Hoeffding bands; endpoint computation optimizes over the entire simultaneous rectangle.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 identifies group--time average treatment effects using never-treated or not-yet-treated comparison groups under limited anticipation and the corresponding parallel-trends condition.
Section 4.2 derives staggered bounds using never-treated controls and observes that not-yet-treated comparisons require accounting for anticipation in the comparison group.
The paper derives anticipation bounds beginning with a classical two-period difference-in-differences model and gives a staggered extension focused on anticipation within treated cohorts.
The paper characterizes anticipation and timing-misclassification bias and constructs corrected estimators using groups known to be unaffected by misspecification.
The paper proves sharp partial-identification results by extending compatible lower-dimensional subdistributions to observationally equivalent full distributions.
Section 2 represents two-way fixed effects by an oriented incidence matrix and treats connected components through separate gauges.
The paper studies estimation and pointwise inference for sharp bounds that are values of generic linear programs, including multiple optima and failures of ordinary bootstrap regularity.
The paper derives asymptotic Gaussian-process simultaneous bands for an entire functional event-study path.

tldr: Announced staggered policies can make one future-treated cohort serve as an anticipatory comparison in several Callaway--Sant'Anna risk sets. Each implementation date is attached deterministically to one known complete path with a fixed earlier announcement date, no implementation before the cohort date, and absorbing implementation thereafter; the reference path has neither announcement nor implementation. Under a proposal-specific all-cohort additive mean restriction for the reference-path means and preregistered edgewise intervals for announcement-to-implementation responses, the reusable pre-implementation means form an edge vector whose admissible distortions are exactly an interval box intersected with the fundamental-cycle equations of the cohort--time graph. The project derives the fiber dimension on its minimal box face, proves that full box variation independence holds exactly when every positive-width edge is a bridge, characterizes nominal endpoint attainment by negative-cycle feasibility, and reduces every signed ATT aggregate endpoint to minimum-cost transshipment. The anchored zero-anticipation corner and a fully specified rational three-cohort contraction provide exact sanity reductions. Bounded potential outcomes are handled by an augmented interval-tension graph. The load-bearing open question is a regime-path-indexed completion theorem lifting every feasible mean vector to one common law of all path potential outcomes. Conditional on that completion, the affine region is causally sharp, and simultaneous Hoeffding bands yield a finite-sample honest outer confidence set by one joint optimization.

project_justification.gap: Callaway--Sant'Anna not-yet-treated comparisons reuse future-treated cohorts, but their point-identification result moves the base period outside a known anticipation horizon. Fenaroli's August 2026 Section 4.2 fixes never-treated controls and observes that not-yet-treated comparisons require accounting for anticipation in the comparison group. Existing bounded-anticipation work therefore supplies neither the joint compatibility restrictions across reused cohort--time means nor a full-law sharpness construction for that setting.
project_justification.niche: A deterministic, known canonical path for each implementation cohort makes the anticipated intervention well defined. The proposal-specific all-cohort additive mean restriction turns the no-announcement reference-path mean surface into an incidence-potential model, while separately calibrated edgewise intervals encode responses between the known announcement and implementation dates without importing Fenaroli's cohort-level increment bounds. Cycles rather than individual contrasts then determine compatibility, bridges determine variation independence, and arbitrary ATT weights become node demands in a transshipment problem.
project_justification.fill: The project gives a basis-invariant cycle theorem with a minimal-face affine-dimension formula, bridge and endpoint if-and-only-if frontiers, a bounded-outcome completion polyhedron, a min-cost-transshipment endpoint formula, and finite-sample outer coverage. Its anchored zero-anticipation formula and complete rational three-cohort instance make the normalization and contraction claims directly auditable. It isolates the only nonalgebraic step as an explicit full-law completion question over all canonical regime paths rather than assuming causal attainability.

related_work: CallawaySantAnna2021, Assumption 3 and Theorem 1, provides the not-yet-treated risk-set functional and the aggregation workflow consumed here; it removes anticipated cells through a known horizon rather than imposing the proposal-specific all-cohort additive mean restriction or bounding jointly reused contaminated cells. Fenaroli2026, Section 4.2, obtains cohortwise staggered bounds with never-treated controls and observes that using not-yet-treated comparisons requires accounting for anticipation in the comparison group. Its cohort-level increment bounds inform sensitivity calibration but are distinct from the edgewise path-response intervals imposed here, and Section 4.2 does not derive common cycle restrictions across reused comparison cells. Gong2022 builds anticipation bounds in a classical potential-outcomes DiD model and later considers staggered adoption, but its first changed proof step does not impose common cycle restrictions across overlapping comparison risk sets. AugustinGutknechtLiu2025 treats anticipation as timing misspecification, uses unaffected groups for correction, and documents the Indonesian anti-cheating application; magnitude-bounded contaminated comparison cohorts remain outside its correction strategy. PiccininniTchetgenStensrud2025 distinguishes interventions on policy decisions from interventions on implementation and motivates indexing potential outcomes by a fully specified deterministic path rather than by an implementation date alone. Torgovitsky2019 shows that a sharp low-dimensional characterization requires an observationally equivalent full-distribution extension, which is the completion obligation isolated here. Dawid2001 supplies the product-range definition of variation independence. JochmansWeidner2019 supplies the incidence, connectivity, and component-gauge language for two-way fixed effects. ChenKyngLiuPengProbstGutenbergSachdeva2022 formalizes minimum-cost flow through incidence balance, capacity, and cost constraints; the present work derives those objects from ATT weights and anticipation intervals. Voronin2025 analyzes generic stochastic LP values and active-face nonregularity, while the finite-sample theorem here avoids endpoint bootstrapping by propagating one simultaneous primitive-mean event. FangLiebl2026 constructs asymptotic simultaneous event-study bands; it does not cover a cycle-coupled identified region in finite samples.
technical_internal_limitation: The exhaustive early kill test is computational evidence, not a proof. All 511 nonempty bipartite graphs with at most three cohorts and three periods were evaluated under randomly generated rational half-grid centers, positive and zero interval widths, disconnected components, feasible mean vectors, and deliberately perturbed mean vectors. Across 1,022 feasibility cases, the direct cycle-fiber linear program, node-potential interval-tension program, and negative-cycle certificate agreed. Across 299 feasible signed support cases, the direct fiber optimum, node-potential optimum, and split-flow transshipment dual agreed to numerical tolerance. No mismatch occurred. The test does not establish the announced-policy causal-completion property.
honest_scope: The cycle-fiber, minimal-face affine dimension, bridge frontier, endpoint certificate, transshipment dual, and finite-sample mean-band propagation are theorem targets. The dimension uses \(\mathcal I(\mu)\), not every positive-width primitive coordinate, whenever feasibility forces the fiber onto a proper box face. The zero-anticipation reduction is asserted only under the explicit rectangular risk-set anchor \(\mathsf{RA}\); without that anchor a target cohort gauge may remain unidentified. Theorems 4--6 are explicitly conditional on resolving Open-ended Question 1, and the predicate \(\mathsf{Comp}_3(z)\) records rather than assumes the worked instance's potential-outcome completion target. Bounded outcome support is enforced on every no-announcement reference-path cohort--time mean through the augmented complete bipartite tension graph, so the proposal does not infer a bounded full law from cycle equations alone. The mapping \(r\mapsto p^r\), every announcement date \(\mathsf a(r)\), and every edgewise sensitivity interval are fixed before outcome analysis. Within-cohort variation in announcement timing or content would require an observed path variable and a different model and is outside this proposal. Statistical learning of sensitivity magnitudes, covariate-conditional versions, continuous treatment timing, endogenous announcements, and uniform optimality of the outer confidence set are also outside scope.
novelty_justification: Callaway and Sant'Anna point-identify not-yet-treated risk-set effects by moving outside a known anticipation horizon. Fenaroli's August 5, 2026 revision derives staggered bounds with never-treated controls; Section 4.2 observes that not-yet-treated comparisons require accounting for anticipation in the comparison group but does not characterize the joint restrictions produced by their reuse across risk sets. The proposed kernel addresses that narrower gap using one deterministic, known announcement-and-implementation path for each cohort, a proposal-specific all-cohort additive mean restriction for the path with neither announcement nor implementation, and edgewise sensitivity intervals for announcement-to-implementation responses that are distinct from Fenaroli's cohort-level increment bounds. The resulting interval-constrained fundamental-cycle fiber has positive-width coordinates that are variation independent if and only if they are bridges, nominal endpoint attainability certified by negative cycles, and arbitrary signed ATT support values given by min-cost transshipment. Torgovitsky and Piccininni show why the remaining full-law completion over explicitly indexed paths cannot be replaced by mean-level LP attainability; the core therefore exposes that construction as its load-bearing open question.
message: Revised the full core with fixed known regime paths, path-indexed potential outcomes, announcement-date-based anticipation cells, synchronized estimands and completion claims, and preserved conditional scope. Schema, dependency closure, proposal-gate, and LaTeX compilation checks pass.
